messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: naming and capitalization
parts:
For a light diversion, let's first decide on capitalization.
The viable pairs in my mind are:

STAN / RSTAN

a. Stan / RStan
b. Stan / R2Stan

c. Stan / rstan
d. Stan / r2stan

e. stan / rstan
f. stan / r2stan

I want to be consistent in our docs and on the web site.
I'm OK with any of a, b, e, or f, but could be convinced
to go with c or d.

I'm happy to decide myself if nobody cares.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] naming and capitalization
parts:
Are we talking about in general, or in executables? I'm inclined to
say Stan when talking about the project/package as a whole, but agree
that typing capitals is exhausting. (I get exhausted easily.) Cf.
Matlab the product versus matlab the executable. Or Java the
programming language versus java/javac the command line executable. Or
Google the company versus google.com and the verb "to google." Etc.

Basically, it seems to me like in prose Stan should get its due as a
proper noun, capital-wise, but that carrying that over to the
computational environment (executable names, CRAN, directory
structures, etc.) is a bit much, since as Andrew mentioned it's a pain
to remember arbitrary (library(RStan)? library(Rstan)?
library(rstan)?) capitalization schemes, and as I mentioned my fingers
get lazy when I'm coding.

However, this is not a position in whose defense I would give up my life.

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] naming and capitalization
parts:
I hadn't realized how much sense it made to
allow both! The reason I wasn't so keen on
"stan" is that it looks terrible in running
text and I've been writing the manual.

All of our running in-text use is caps, including
on the web page and in the doc.

The only executable so far is "stanc".

The C++ namespace is "stan".

The Google Code project name is "stan".

The logo is "STAN".

And we'll go with "rstan" for the official
package name in R, so that'd be library("rstan").
(The problem is that so many packages do this
a different way that any choice is in effect
arbitrary.)

- Bob
